_about: The armor and the struggle side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of struggle against evil powers that more than one book shares, beginning with the armor of Ephesians 6 and the places that share its words, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme's own outline cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: Put on the armor

The Law & history: The one putting on his armor should not boast like one taking it off
put a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in armor
Gospels & Acts: he takes away the armor in which the man trusted
The letters: Put on the full armor of God, so that you can make your stand against the devil's schemes
take up the full armor of God
lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light

rows.alike: Ephesians and Romans both tell the readers to "put on" armor: "the full armor of God" and "the armor of light".
rows.different: Ephesians 6:11 gives the reason "so that you can make your stand against the devil's schemes"; Romans 13:12 sets the armor against "the deeds of darkness". In Luke 11:22 armor is taken away: "the armor in which the man trusted". The asides speak of soldiers' armor.

rows.title: A belt around the waist

The Prophets: Righteousness will be the belt around His hips, and faithfulness the sash around His waist
The letters: with the belt of truth buckled around your waist

rows.alike: Both name a quality worn as a belt: "Righteousness will be the belt around His hips", "the belt of truth buckled around your waist".
rows.different: Isaiah 11:5 speaks of "His hips" and "His waist" and names "Righteousness" and "faithfulness"; Ephesians 6:14 is said to the readers ("your waist") and names "truth", giving righteousness to the breastplate instead.

rows.title: The breastplate of righteousness

The Law & history: the ephod itself, and the breastplate
The Prophets: He put on righteousness like a breastplate
The letters: with the breastplate of righteousness arrayed
putting on the breastplate of faith and love
Revelation: They also had breastplates like breastplates of iron

rows.alike: Isaiah 59:17 and Ephesians 6:14 join righteousness and the breastplate: "He put on righteousness like a breastplate", "the breastplate of righteousness". 1 Thessalonians 5:8 also speaks of "putting on the breastplate".
rows.different: In Isaiah 59:17 it is "He" who "put on righteousness like a breastplate", with "the helmet of salvation on His head"; Ephesians 6:14 ("your waist") and 1 Thessalonians 5:8 ("let us be sober, putting on the breastplate") are said to the readers. 1 Thessalonians 5:8 names "faith and love" for the breastplate, not righteousness. The asides are the breastplate Aaron is clothed with in Exodus 29:5 and the "breastplates of iron" of Revelation 9:9.

rows.title: Feet that bring the good news of peace

The Prophets: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace
the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace!
The letters: As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!
your feet fitted with the readiness of the gospel of peace

rows.alike: Each speaks of feet and good news: "the feet of those who bring good news", "your feet fitted with the readiness of the gospel of peace". Isaiah, Nahum and Ephesians add peace: "who proclaim peace", "who proclaims peace", "the gospel of peace".
rows.different: Isaiah 52:7 has the feet "on the mountains"; Nahum 1:15 says "Look to the mountains". Isaiah's messengers "proclaim salvation" and "say to Zion"; Nahum's verse goes on "Celebrate your feasts, O Judah". Romans 10:15 sets "As it is written" after "how can they preach unless they are sent?"; Ephesians 6:15 speaks of the readers' own feet, "fitted with the readiness".

rows.title: A shield

The Law & history: I am your shield, your very great reward
He is the shield that protects you, the sword in which you boast
Psalms & wisdom: You, O LORD, are a shield around me
The LORD is my strength and my shield
Take up Your shield and buckler
His faithfulness is a shield and rampart
He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him
The letters: take up the shield of faith

rows.alike: Each speaks of a shield, and two of taking one up: "Take up Your shield and buckler", "take up the shield of faith".
rows.different: In Genesis 15:1, Deuteronomy 33:29, Psalm 3:3 and Psalm 28:7 the shield is the LORD himself ("I am your shield", "He is the shield that protects you", "You, O LORD, are a shield around me", "The LORD is my strength and my shield"); Psalm 91:4 has "His faithfulness is a shield and rampart" and Proverbs 30:5 "He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him". Psalm 35:2 asks "Take up Your shield and buckler". In Ephesians 6:16 the readers are told to "take up the shield of faith".

rows.title: Flaming arrows

Psalms & wisdom: There He shattered the flaming arrows, the shield and sword and weapons of war
He ordains His arrows with fire
Like a madman shooting firebrands and deadly arrows
The letters: with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one

rows.alike: Psalm 76:3 and Ephesians 6:16 name "the flaming arrows", and Psalm 7:13 "His arrows with fire".
rows.different: In Psalm 76:3 "He shattered the flaming arrows" along with "the shield and sword and weapons of war"; in Psalm 7:13 the arrows are "His arrows", ordained "with fire". Ephesians 6:16 speaks of "the flaming arrows of the evil one", which "you can extinguish" with the shield of faith.

rows.title: The helmet of salvation

The Prophets: the helmet of salvation on His head
The letters: the helmet of our hope of salvation

rows.alike: Isaiah 59:17 and Ephesians 6:17 say "the helmet of salvation" in the same words; 1 Thessalonians 5:8 says "the helmet of our hope of salvation".
rows.different: Isaiah 59:17 has the helmet "on His head", with "garments of vengeance" and "a cloak of zeal", which Ephesians 6:17 and 1 Thessalonians 5:8 do not name. Ephesians 6:17 says "take the helmet of salvation"; 1 Thessalonians 5:8 says "putting on" it, and adds "our hope of".

rows.title: The word of God and the double-edged sword

The Law & history: Ehud had made for himself a double-edged sword a cubit long
Psalms & wisdom: May the high praises of God be in their mouths, and a double-edged sword in their hands
The letters: the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God
the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword
Revelation: a sharp double-edged sword came from His mouth
These are the words of the One who holds the sharp, double-edged sword

rows.alike: Ephesians 6:17 and Hebrews 4:12 set "the word of God" beside a sword: "the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God", "Sharper than any double-edged sword". Psalm 149:6 sets "the high praises of God" beside "a double-edged sword". Revelation 1:16 has "a sharp double-edged sword came from His mouth", and Revelation 2:12 has "the words of the One who holds the sharp, double-edged sword".
rows.different: Ephesians 6:17 calls "the sword of the Spirit" "the word of God"; Hebrews 4:12 says "the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword" and "It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart". Psalm 149:6 puts "the high praises of God" "in their mouths" and "a double-edged sword in their hands". Proverbs 5:4 has "sharp as a double-edged sword" of "she", "in the end"; Judges 3:16 says "Ehud had made for himself a double-edged sword a cubit long".

rows.title: Watch and pray

The Law & history: So we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night
Gospels & Acts: Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation
Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation
keep watch at all times, and pray
The letters: stay alert with all perseverance in your prayers for all the saints
Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful
be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray

rows.alike: Most join praying with keeping watch: "Watch and pray", "keep watch at all times, and pray", "stay alert with all perseverance in your prayers", "prayed to our God and posted a guard".
rows.different: Nehemiah 4:9 has "we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night". Matthew and Mark add "so that you will not enter into temptation"; Luke 21:36 "that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen"; Ephesians 6:18 asks for prayers "for all the saints"; Colossians adds "thankful". 1 Peter 4:7 says "be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray", and does not say watch.

rows.title: Be strong

The Law & history: David found strength in the LORD his God
Psalms & wisdom: Be strong and courageous, all you who hope in the LORD
You have armed me with strength for battle
The Prophets: be strong, all you people of the land
The letters: be strong in the Lord and in His mighty power
Be men of courage. Be strong.
be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus

rows.alike: "Be strong" is said in the Law and history, the Psalms, the Prophets and the letters, most often joined with courage: "be strong and courageous" (Deuteronomy 31:6, Joshua 1:9, Psalm 31:24 and others), "Be men of courage. Be strong." (1 Corinthians 16:13). Ephesians 6:10, 2 Timothy 2:1 and Haggai 2:4 say "be strong" without courage.
rows.different: Some say where the strength is: "in the Lord and in His mighty power" (Ephesians 6:10), "in the grace that is in Christ Jesus" (2 Timothy 2:1), "in the LORD his God" (1 Samuel 30:6). Many give a reason: "the LORD your God is with you wherever you go" (Joshua 1:9), "I will be with you" (Deuteronomy 31:23), "there is a greater One with us than with him" (2 Chronicles 32:7), "I am with you" (Haggai 2:4); Joshua 10:25 says "the LORD will do this to all the enemies you fight". Several add "Do not be afraid or discouraged" (Joshua 10:25, 1 Chronicles 22:13, 28:20, 2 Chronicles 32:7). Psalm 27:14 sets it beside "Wait patiently for the LORD" and Psalm 31:24 says it to "all you who hope in the LORD". Psalm 18:39 is said to one addressed as "You": "You have armed me with strength for battle".

rows.title: Stand firm

The Law & history: Stand firm and you will see the LORD's salvation
stand firm, and see the salvation of the LORD on your behalf
The Prophets: If you do not stand firm in your faith, then you will not stand at all
The letters: you will be able to stand your ground, and having done everything, to stand
you stand firm in one spirit

rows.alike: "Stand firm" in each column; Isaiah 7:9, 1 Corinthians 16:13 and 1 Peter 5:9 join it to faith: "stand firm in your faith", "Stand firm in the faith", "standing firm in your faith".
rows.different: In Exodus 14:13 and 2 Chronicles 20:17 those who stand firm will "see" the LORD's salvation, and 2 Chronicles says "You need not fight this battle". Isaiah 7:9 warns "then you will not stand at all". Ephesians 6:13 ties standing to "the full armor of God" and "the day of evil"; 1 Peter 5:9 says "Resist him, standing firm in your faith".

rows.title: Not according to the flesh: the weapons of the warfare

Psalms & wisdom: Wisdom is better than weapons of war
The Prophets: No weapon formed against you shall prosper
The letters: our struggle is not against flesh and blood
we do not wage war according to the flesh
The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the flesh. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds
with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left

rows.alike: Weapons are set beside something other than themselves: "Wisdom is better than weapons of war", "No weapon formed against you shall prosper", "The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the flesh".
rows.different: Ecclesiastes and Isaiah speak of weapons of war and of weapons "formed against you"; 2 Corinthians speaks of "our" weapons, which "have divine power to demolish strongholds", and of "the weapons of righteousness". Ephesians 6:12 says whom the struggle is not against: "flesh and blood".

rows.title: Fight the good fight, fight the LORD's battles

The Law & history: Only be valiant for me and fight the LORD's battles
because he fights the LORD's battles
The letters: so that by them you may fight the good fight
Fight the good fight of the faith
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith
like a good soldier of Christ Jesus

rows.alike: Each speaks of fighting and names it: "fight the LORD's battles", "Fight the good fight of the faith".
rows.different: 1 Samuel 18:17 is said to David, and sets Saul's thought beside it: "let the hand of the Philistines be against him"; 1 Samuel 25:28 says "because he fights the LORD's battles" of "my lord", in words that begin "Please forgive your servant's offense". In the letters it is "the good fight of the faith", charged to Timothy ("Timothy, my child") and said of himself by the writer: "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith".

rows.title: The rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms

The letters: against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this world's darkness, and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms
made known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms
far above all rule and authority, power and dominion
whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities. All things were created through Him and for Him
having disarmed the powers and authorities
with angels, authorities, and powers subject to Him

rows.alike: The letters name "rulers" and "authorities" together, with "powers", "dominions" and "principalities".
rows.different: Ephesians 6:12 names them as those "our struggle" is against, "in the heavenly realms"; Ephesians 3:10 says God's wisdom is "made known to" them; Colossians 1:16 says "All things were created through Him and for Him"; Colossians 2:15 says "having disarmed the powers and authorities"; 1 Peter 3:22 says "subject to Him". Luke 12:11 and Titus 3:1 use the words of the rulers before whom believers are brought and to whom they "submit".

rows.title: Resist the devil

The Prophets: the people who know their God will firmly resist him
Gospels & Acts: he left Him until an opportune time
The letters: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you
Resist him, standing firm in your faith
do not give the devil a foothold
make your stand against the devil's schemes
we are not unaware of his schemes

rows.alike: James and 1 Peter say "Resist the devil" and "Resist him"; James adds "he will flee from you".
rows.different: James sets "Submit yourselves, then, to God" before the command; 1 Peter adds "standing firm in your faith". Matthew 4:11 and Luke 4:13 say "the devil left Him"; Matthew goes on "and angels came and ministered to Him", Luke "until an opportune time"; neither verse says "resist". Ephesians and 2 Corinthians speak of "the devil's schemes" and "his schemes". Daniel 11:32 says "the people who know their God will firmly resist him", after "With flattery he will corrupt those who violate the covenant".

rows.title: Satan before the LORD, at the right hand to accuse

Psalms & wisdom: the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them
Satan also came with them to present himself before Him
let an accuser stand at his right hand
The Prophets: with Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him

rows.alike: Satan is named in Job and Zechariah: "Satan also came with them to present himself before Him", "with Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him". Psalm 109:6 and Zechariah 3:1 share "at his right hand" and an accuser: "let an accuser stand at his right hand".
rows.different: In Job 1:6 and 2:1 Satan comes "with" "the sons of God" "before the LORD"; in Zechariah 3:1 Satan stands "at his right hand" beside "Joshua the high priest", who is "standing before the angel of the LORD". Psalm 109:6 is worded "let an accuser stand at his right hand" and goes with "Set over him a wicked man".

rows.title: Incited, stirred up

The Law & history: Then Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to take a census of Israel
the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He stirred up David against them
Psalms & wisdom: even though you incited Me against him to ruin him without cause

rows.alike: Each says someone was incited or stirred up: "incited David to take a census of Israel", "He stirred up David against them", "you incited Me against him".
rows.different: The two accounts of David's census name different subjects: 2 Samuel 24:1 says "the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He stirred up David"; 1 Chronicles 21:1 says "Satan rose up against Israel and incited David". In Job 2:3 the LORD says to Satan "you incited Me against him".

rows.title: Rebuked

Gospels & Acts: He rebuked the demons and would not allow them to speak
rebuked Peter and said, “Get behind Me, Satan!
The letters: did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him, but said, “The Lord rebuke you!

rows.alike: A rebuke in each: "The LORD rebukes you, Satan!", "The Lord rebuke you!", "Jesus rebuked the spirit".
rows.different: In Zechariah 3:2 the LORD speaks: "The LORD rebukes you, Satan!"; in Jude 1:9 "the archangel Michael" says "The Lord rebuke you!" to the devil and "did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him". In the Gospels Jesus rebukes spirits and demons Himself, and in Mark 8:33 He rebukes Peter with "Get behind Me, Satan!".

rows.title: Unclean spirits commanded to come out

The Prophets: I will also remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land
Gospels & Acts: He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him!
Come out of this man, you unclean spirit!
Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man
Jesus gave them authority over unclean spirits
giving them authority over unclean spirits
Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.
In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!
I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.
Revelation: three unclean spirits that looked like frogs

rows.alike: "The spirit of impurity" is named in Zechariah 13:2, "three unclean spirits" in Revelation 16:13 and "unclean spirits" in the Gospels; in the Gospels and Acts spirits are commanded: "He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him!", "In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!".
rows.different: Zechariah 13:2 says the LORD will "remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land", with the names of the idols. Revelation 16:13 sees "three unclean spirits" coming "out of the mouths of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet". Jesus gives "authority over unclean spirits" to the Twelve; Paul commands "In the name of Jesus Christ"; the itinerant Jewish exorcists of Acts 19 say "I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims".

rows.title: The finger of God

The Law & history: This is the finger of God
tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God
inscribed by the finger of God
Gospels & Acts: But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you
But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you

rows.alike: Exodus 8:19 and Luke 11:20 both speak of "the finger of God": "This is the finger of God", "if I drive out demons by the finger of God".
rows.different: In Exodus 8:19 "the magicians said to Pharaoh", and "Pharaoh's heart was hardened". Luke 11:20 has it of driving out demons, where Matthew 12:28 has "by the Spirit of God". The asides use the words of the stone tablets "inscribed by the finger of God".

rows.title: Michael

The Prophets: Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me
no one has the courage to support me against these, except Michael your prince
Michael, the great prince who stands watch over your people, will rise up
The letters: the archangel Michael, when he disputed with the devil over the body of Moses
Revelation: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon

rows.alike: Michael is named in each: "came to help me", "disputed with the devil", "fought against the dragon".
rows.different: Daniel calls him "one of the chief princes", "your prince" and "the great prince who stands watch over your people", and the one opposing is "the prince of the kingdom of Persia"; Jude calls him "the archangel" and names "the devil"; Revelation says "Michael and his angels" and names "the dragon".

rows.title: The prince of this world, the god of this age

Gospels & Acts: now the prince of this world will be cast out
the prince of this world is coming, and he has no claim on Me
the prince of this world has been condemned
The letters: The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers
the ruler of the power of the air, the spirit who is now at work in the sons of disobedience
the whole world is under the power of the evil one

rows.alike: Each speaks of a power in "this world", "this age" or "the whole world": "the prince of this world", "The god of this age", "the ruler of the power of the air", "the whole world is under the power of the evil one".
rows.different: John's three verses use only "the prince of this world", and speak of the prince as "cast out", having "no claim on Me", and "condemned". Each letter has its own words: "The god of this age", who "has blinded the minds of unbelievers"; "the ruler of the power of the air", "now at work in the sons of disobedience"; "the evil one".

rows.title: Kept from the evil one

Psalms & wisdom: The LORD will guard you from all evil
Gospels & Acts: deliver us from the evil one
keep them from the evil one
The letters: He will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one
the One who was born of God protects him, and the evil one cannot touch him
the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one

rows.alike: Each asks, promises or provides keeping: "guard you from all evil", "guard you from the evil one", "keep them from the evil one", "deliver us from the evil one", "the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one" (Ephesians 6:16).
rows.different: Psalm 121:7 says "all evil"; the others say "the evil one". Matthew 6:13 asks "deliver us from the evil one"; John 17:15 says "I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one"; Psalm 121 and 2 Thessalonians promise; 1 John 5:18 says "the evil one cannot touch him"; Ephesians 6:16 speaks of "the shield of faith".

rows.title: The snare: escaped

Psalms & wisdom: Surely He will deliver you from the snare of the fowler
We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowler
The letters: so that he will not fall into disgrace and into the snare of the devil
escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to his will

rows.alike: A snare, and escape from it: "We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowler", "escape the snare of the devil".
rows.different: The Psalms say "the snare of the fowler", and Psalm 91:3 that "He will deliver you"; the letters say "the snare of the devil", and 2 Timothy 2:26 adds "who has taken them captive to his will".

rows.title: Tempted

Gospels & Acts: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil
He was there for forty days, being tempted by Satan
for forty days He was tempted by the devil
The letters: for fear that the tempter had somehow tempted you
so that Satan will not tempt you through your lack of self-control
He Himself suffered when He was tempted
one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin

rows.alike: Temptation is named in each, and in most a tempter: "to be tempted by the devil", "being tempted by Satan", "the tempter had somehow tempted you", "He Himself suffered when He was tempted".
rows.different: The Gospels tell of Jesus in the wilderness "for forty days". 1 Thessalonians 3:5 has "for fear that the tempter had somehow tempted you" and 1 Corinthians 7:5 "so that Satan will not tempt you". Hebrews 4:15 says "one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin", and Hebrews 2:18 and 4:15 name no tempter.

rows.title: Overcome

Gospels & Acts: take courage; I have overcome the world!
The letters: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good
you have overcome the evil one
have overcome them, because greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world
this is the victory that has overcome the world: our faith
you have overcome the evil one
Revelation: The one who overcomes will not be harmed by the second death
They have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony

rows.alike: Each speaks of overcoming: "I have overcome the world!", "you have overcome the evil one", "The one who overcomes", "They have conquered him".
rows.different: What is overcome differs: "the world" (John 16:33, 1 John 5:4), "evil" (Romans 12:21), "the evil one" (1 John 2:13, 2:14), "them" (1 John 4:4), "him" (Revelation 12:11). How differs too: "with good", "our faith", "because greater is He who is in you", "by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony", and in 1 John 2:14 "the word of God abides in you".

rows.title: Trodden under your feet

The Law & history: you shall trample their high places
Psalms & wisdom: You will tread on the lion and cobra; you will trample the young lion and serpent
The Prophets: you will trample the wicked, for they will be ashes under the soles of your feet
Gospels & Acts: I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy
The letters: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet

rows.alike: Treading and trampling underfoot: "You will tread on the lion and cobra", "authority to tread on snakes and scorpions", "under the soles of your feet", "crush Satan under your feet".
rows.different: What is trodden differs: "their high places", "the lion and cobra ... the young lion and serpent", "the wicked", "snakes and scorpions, and ... all the power of the enemy", "Satan". In Romans 16:20 "The God of peace" does the crushing; in the others the hearers tread.

rows.title: Children of the devil

Gospels & Acts: You belong to your father, the devil
He was a murderer from the beginning
The weeds are the sons of the evil one
O child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness
The letters: the children of God are distinguished from the children of the devil
The one who practices sin is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the very start
Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother

rows.alike: Some are called the devil's: "your father, the devil", "child of the devil", "the children of the devil", "the sons of the evil one", "belonged to the evil one". John 8:44 and 1 John 3:8 both say "from the beginning" or "from the very start".
rows.different: John 8:44 calls the devil "a murderer from the beginning" and "the father of lies"; Acts 13:10 says "O child of the devil and enemy of all righteousness"; Matthew 13:38 sets "The weeds are the sons of the evil one" beside "the good seed represents the sons of the kingdom"; 1 John 3:10 says how they are "distinguished", "Anyone who does not practice righteousness", and 3:12 names "Cain".

rows.title: The power of darkness

Gospels & Acts: this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness
turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God
The letters: He has rescued us from the dominion of darkness
the powers of this world's darkness
lay aside the deeds of darkness
Have no fellowship with the fruitless deeds of darkness, but rather expose them

rows.alike: Darkness is named as a power or dominion: "the power of darkness", "the dominion of darkness", "the powers of this world's darkness"; Acts 26:18 sets "darkness" beside "the power of Satan".
rows.different: Luke 22:53 has "this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness", after "you did not lay a hand on Me". Acts 26:18 and Colossians 1:13 speak of a turning or rescue, "from darkness to light", "into the kingdom of His beloved Son". Romans 13:12 and Ephesians 5:11 speak of "deeds of darkness" to lay aside or expose.

owner_review: Doug saw the front page and the table in the preview, 2026-10-07: 'trinity, spiritual warfare, children of God approved'
